summary: preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React UI component extension library, but its package.json declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs is written with hex-mangled identifiers and property-lookup indirection (e.g. `_0x488df8`, `_0x19328d.WuGMv="musl"`, `_0x19328d.TdVzu="/etc/os-release"`), fingerprints the installer's libc/distro via `execFileSync("ldd", ["--version"])` and by reading `/etc/os-release` to detect musl/Alpine, then constructs a URL of the form `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/<variant>.zip` (selecting `bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline` on Alpine), downloads and extracts the Bun runtime, `chmod`s it to 0755, and finally runs `execFileSync(bun, ["math_init.js"])`. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle with a shuffled string-array decoder (`WV8StW` performs `push(shift())` rotation over a large mixed numeric/string array), so its behavior is not auditable from shipped source. The net effect on `npm install` is: fetch an alien runtime from a non-registry host and use it to execute a heavily-obfuscated bundled script on the installer's machine. A React component library has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime or an obfuscated multi-hundred-KB blob at install time, and executing the payload under Bun bypasses Node-based install-time inspection. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper shape (obfuscated loader + alien-runtime execution of an opaque payload at preinstall) with a stated package purpose that does not justify any of it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
